modelingNotes: The complete OSM outline fixes the hall plan, including projecting structural piers. The outline height of 34 m sets the main roof; the four mapped roof structures retain their 38/40 m tops.

The reviewed CC BY 2.0 photograph references/03.jpg establishes a broad industrial hall with exposed roof trusses, tall glazed bays and a regular structural rhythm. References 01/02 confirm the long elevation. Truss section, 5.4 m depth, 16 m panel rhythm and glazing dimensions are map-scale inferences, not survey measurements.

Four longitudinal roof truss lines follow the three-bay width of the plan. The material library roof grey substitutes for painted blue steel; windows and mapped rooflights use the approved light-blue palette.

The two mapped circular roof structures begin at the roof datum rather than becoming enclosed cylinders through the interior. The Geode, reflecting pools, bridges and landscaping lie outside this footprint and are omitted.
No photographic textures or interiors. Fine screen mesh, pipework and mullions are reduced to sparse facade divisions; roof trusses remain open geometry.

modelingNotes: The OSM outline fixes the palace, lateral galleries and semicircular rear courtyard, preserving its central void. The mapped gallery part is 7 m tall; the remaining palace uses the outline 13 m height.

The inspected CC0 photo references/00.jpg establishes the garden front with three monumental glazed arches, engaged columns, strong horizontal cornices, roof parapet and lower columned wings. Main facade arch/pier dimensions are proportional inferences fitted to the mapped south facade.

The mapped low gallery is represented as an open colonnade beneath its continuous 7 m roof. Repeated column locations and semicircular gallery rhythm are inferred from the plan and visible lateral colonnade; the rear side is not shown by the selected photograph.

The wall plane is set 0.45 m inside the mapped outer ornament envelope to expose engaged columns; foundation, parapet and roof retain the mapped extremities. The palace roof is a flat grey surface enclosed by a shallow stone parapet. Balustrade sculpture, inscriptions, fine capitals and ironwork are omitted. Windows use the standard light-blue palette; no photographic textures are used.

modelingNotes: The saved OSM footprint and 47 height-tagged parts define the 60 m pyramidal bell tower, 26.8 m nave/apse, low aisles, chapels and buttresses. Many chapel heights carry IGN Lidar HD provenance; original roof directions and heights are retained.

One 10.5 square metre mapped part has no height; it remains represented only by the common foundation rather than inventing a volume. Hidden internal part intersections are not a watertight building interior.

Inspected eligible references 00,03,06 confirm the tall square Romanesque tower with paired rounded bell bays, steep slate spire, long nave clerestory and attached lower street-front buildings. Bell windows, nave rhythm, stone ledges and clock are schematic map-scale inferences.

Skillion roofs include hidden stone undersides to make their volume closed and normal orientation unambiguous; no exposed sloped roofs face downward. Window and bell-bay panels use the shared light-blue window material and are clipped to actual constructed walls. Fine louvres, sculpture, clock ornament, roof crosses and individual masonry are omitted. Grey roof material substitutes for the photographed slate color.
